core.title: Declare the composition-root layer in every journey spec header
core.given: A journey spec: a test file matching the stack's e2e-test name patterns that the stack's test runner actually runs, OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey or user/system flow binding, outside the stack's never-scanned vendored and generated trees.
core.when: The spec exists in the scanned tree — whether newly created, already present, or edited in any way (header or body).
core.then: The spec's header block MUST carry the layer declaration naming the composition root.
prefer: Add the composition-root layer declaration to the spec's header block.
Treat a test file that carries journey or user/system flow header bindings under another name as a journey spec and give it the composition-root layer declaration.
avoid: Omitting the layer declaration from a journey spec header.
Declaring a single layer role (e.g. presentation or application) on a journey spec because it mainly exercises that layer.
Renaming a journey spec away from the stack's e2e-test name pattern or stripping its journey bindings to escape the check.
unless: Vendored and generated trees (the stack-wide never-scanned list) are never scanned.
core.why: A journey test exercises the assembled application, not a single layer of it; a missing or wrong layer declaration routes the result to the wrong layer bucket.
evidence: Every in-scope spec — each runner-run e2e-test file and each test file with a journey or user/system flow header binding, outside never-scanned trees — carries the composition-root layer declaration in its header block.
The stack's check for this rule reports no findings for any in-scope spec.
verification: Scope: test files matching the stack's e2e-test name patterns that the stack's test runner actually runs, plus any test file whose header comments carry a journey or user/system flow binding, so misnamed journey specs are still judged.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey or user/system flow URN in a string literal is not a journey spec; only header bindings count.
Vendored and generated trees (the stack-wide never-scanned list, roots.excluded) are skipped entirely.
Finding when the header's layer declaration is missing or names any layer other than the composition root.
The check judges every in-scope spec whenever scanned, regardless of what change touched the file; the concrete detector, validator and finding ids are realization details of the stack.

A journey spec header declares a single layer role (e.g. application) instead of the composition root.
doesNotFire: A unit test that only mentions a journey or user/system flow URN inside a string literal.
Any file in the stack's never-scanned vendored or generated trees.

A unit test with no journey or user/system flow header bindings and not matching the e2e-test name pattern.

neutralityNotes: The rule neutralizes cleanly. 'Journey spec' is expressed as the e2e-test role plus the profile's e2e-test name pattern and the runner's run set (branch A), or a journey/user-system-flow header binding via urn.binding.user-system-flow / urn.binding.journey (branch B); the ATDD-Bun marker forms (`// UserSystemFlow:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:user-system-flow:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`) are profile values, not core text. The stack's layer value `assembly` is treated as the local name of the composition-root role (roles.composition_root.name, per the vocabulary's own example), and the `// Layer:` header line is the stack's role-assignment idiom (roles.assignment). The never-scanned trees defer to the one stack-wide roots.excluded list, which is a superset of the four trees this rule's text names; that deference is the sanctioned neutralization. Realization-only tokens kept in bunOnly: the detector/validator id htmx_e2e_detector (in activation.facts[3], evidence[1], verifier_detail[4]) and the source term id `browser_spec` (noted in classification, verifier_detail[0]). No proposed keys were needed.
